A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MyScholarQA research. Their main text, figures, tables, and appendices A-D support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures and duplicated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic benchmark evaluations, model ablations, a five-participant formative study, and a 21-participant user study.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark evaluations, ablations, formative study, and user-study results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The profile inference, editable personalized/generic actions, and ScholarQA-based retrieval and report generation remain unchanged. Calling MyScholarQA an 'agent' instead of a 'system' does not introduce a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same ScholarQA-CS2/CS-PaperSum synthetic research-query coverage and the same formative and active-user studies. No dataset, population, domain, or test scenario is added.

E2.justification: The profile/action model comparisons and report baselines remain unchanged, including ScholarQA, OpenScholar, STORM, Perplexity Sonar DR, and OpenAI o3 DR. Table 10 repeats existing comparators.

E3.justification: The synthetic split construction, evaluation metrics, model settings, study procedures, and ten-example o3 DR evaluation are retained. Appendix A's experimental settings are unchanged apart from footnote numbering.

E4.justification: Appendices A.4-A.6 retain the query-similarity analysis, action-placement/model/action-count ablations, and judge-prompt variations. Tables 6-9 and Figures 7-9 preserve the same analyses and findings.

E5.justification: Both versions report single-run results in Appendix A.3 and retain the same agreement reporting and Figure 6 binomial tests with Bonferroni correction. No statistical reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Matched scores, plotted results, error frequencies, and qualitative findings are unchanged, including Table 3's report results and the 73% satisfaction finding. v2's Table 10 reproduces Table 3 with expanded labels.

T1.justification: The added A* ⊆ A notation in Section 2.2 summarizes the retained action-selection description. It introduces no substantive theoretical development; mathematical reasoning, derivations, and proofs do not change.

C1.justification: The four contributions and central argument remain: MyScholarQA performs well under offline evaluation, while real users reveal personalization failures that the tested LLM judges miss.

C2.justification: Section 8 qualifies generalizability: v1 says many insights 'are generalizable,' whereas v2 says they 'may apply generally.' The principal failure interpretations and four design lessons remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 8 adds a URL for the existing Chrome Dino Game used during waiting. This supplies limited additional resource-access information; core implementation settings, prompts, and code/data disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Srikanth et al. (2026), Mondal et al. (2024), Balepur et al. (2025b), and Joachims (2002), and removes Zhao et al. (2021). The overall research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes local copyedits throughout the main text, expands explanatory transitions, and revises acknowledgments and terminology. The section organization and overall narrative remain substantially the same.

P2.justification: Main-text captions are expanded and reformatted, with associated table and figure repositioning. Figures 5 and 6 move to later pages. New Table 10 redisplays Table 3 using fuller model and metric labels.

improvement.justification: Expanded captions and fuller table labels modestly improve readability, while Section 8 more cautiously qualifies generalizability. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, and duplicated Table 10 adds redundancy rather than additional support. Overall, the gains are limited to presentation and qualification of the findings.
